tool_calls.result_text:
v_fpy_daily
  workcell (VARCHAR): Workcell = customer.
  workcell_id (BIGINT): Join key to v_workcell.
  assembly (VARCHAR): Part number = model = assembly.
  model_id (BIGINT): Join key to dim_model.
  step (VARCHAR): The MES test step (ICT, FVT …) where the result was recorded. Only steps that pass boards count as test steps — SCRAP, RTC and BIRTH are dispositions, never tests.
  date (DATE): Local date of the test scan.
  boards_passed (BIGINT): Distinct boards whose FIRST test at this step passed.
  boards_tested (BIGINT): Distinct boards tested at this step, first loop only (test_loop = 1). Retests are excluded — FPY is first pass.
  fpy (DOUBLE): First-pass yield = boards_passed ÷ boards_tested. 'A' (aborted) results are excluded from both.

**Overall First‑Pass Yield (FPY) ≈ 97.1 %** for the period 9 Jul – 22 Aug 2026 (average across all workcells). **Workcells with the lowest average FPY** | Workcell | Avg FPY | |------------------------|--------| | ELENION TECHNOLOGIES | 85.7 % | | GOPRO | 89.5 % | | LIFE360 | 94.7 % | | Nokia Optics | 94.9 % | | INFINERA | 95.4 % | **Actionable levers to lift yield** | Lever | Why it matters | Typical steps | |------|----------------|---------------| | **Target low‑performing workcells** | They pull the plant average down (e.g., ELENION at 85 %). | • Run a detailed FPY root‑cause analysis (defect types, test step failures).
• Verify test equipment calibration and MES scan delta times for those cells.
• Align standard cycle‑time study (v_cycle_time) with actual scan‑based elapsed times to spot bottlenecks. | | **Standard‑time alignment** | Two cycle‑time definitions exist – study (standard work content) vs. MES scan delta (elapsed). Mis‑alignment can hide rework loops that hurt FPY. | • Compare v_cycle_time.standard_time to v_scan_point.elapsed_time for the same workcell/step.
• Adjust work instructions or equipment settings where elapsed > standard + 10 %. | | **Equipment health checks** | Faulty or under‑performing machines increase defect rates. | • Cross‑reference v_equipment scan logs with low‑FPY workcells.
• Schedule preventive maintenance on any equipment showing high scan‑delta variance. | | **Operator training & staffing** | Human error is a common FPY driver. | • Use v_employee and v_headcount to ensure staffing levels meet the standard SMH (standard minutes per hour) for each workcell.
• Conduct refresher training on critical test steps identified in v_fpy_daily. | | **Process step optimization** | Certain test steps have higher failure rates. | • Drill into v_fpy_daily by step (group by workcell, step) to pinpoint “hot” steps.
• Apply DOE (design of experiments) to tweak parameters (e.g., test voltage, timing). | | **Feedback loop to demand planning** | Sudden demand spikes can pressure cells, raising defect rates. | • Align demand (v_demand) with capacity (v_units_out_daily) to avoid over‑loading any workcell.
• If demand exceeds capacity, consider temporary load‑balancing to higher‑FPY cells. | **Next step** – run a focused FPY drill‑down for the three lowest workcells (ELENION, GOPRO, LIFE360) by test step and equipment to prioritize corrective actions.
